results.deviation: The smoothing setting is labelled signal in lower case rather than Signal, because signal is a built-in name in OpenScript, so the setting cannot be assigned to a name of its own and is keyed by its label instead.
The Squeeze On and Squeeze Off states are drawn as red and green line segments along zero rather than as separate dots, because a plot in this OpenScript version has no dots-only style.
The performance table sits in the nearest of the four chart corners and at the chart's own text size, because a table here has no centre or middle positions and no size setting.

The zig zag line is drawn 60 bars behind the newest bar because a plot cannot redraw bars it has already drawn, so the newest 60 bars show no zig zag line and, with a long Zig Zag Length where a swing takes more than 60 bars to settle, parts of the older line can differ from the final swings (signals, level lines and candle colours are unaffected); the table is drawn at the chart's own text size and in the nearest corner, because a table here has no size setting and pins only to a corner.

The fill level lines are drawn on every bar while a side is armed, so they also show levels that a newer displacement candle replaced and levels that were never filled, whereas the original draws a level only from the newest displacement candle to the bar that fills it; whether a level will be filled is known only on the fill bar, and a study cannot go back and blank the bars it has already drawn. Every level shown agrees with the original.

The table is drawn at the chart's own text size whatever Table Size says, and a middle row or centre column is drawn in the nearest corner, because a table here has no size setting and pins only to a corner.

The bar RVOL columns rise from the pane's axis rather than from the baseline of 1, because a plot has no base setting in this OpenScript version; and a time zone name that is not recognised stops the study instead of falling back to America/New_York, because a zone name cannot be checked before it is used.

The midpoint, Fibonacci and previous day and week lines are drawn solid rather than dotted or dashed, because a plot has no dotted or dashed style; the VWAP anchor menu is titled vwapAnchor in the settings dialog, because its setting is filed under its title and vwapAnchor is a built-in name; the acceptance and rejection labels are plain plates at the level price rather than pointed tags, because a drawn label has no pointer shape; and a time zone name that is not recognised stops the study instead of falling back to America/New_York, because a zone name cannot be checked before it is used.

The regime panel always sits in the bottom-right corner at the chart's text size, because a table's corner is fixed before the first bar and a table has no text size; the zone engine walks every bar rather than only the newest Engine history bars, and on a chart that gives no tick size the fallback tick is taken from the latest 50 closes so far rather than the chart's final 50, because a study that runs bar by bar cannot see which bar will be the newest; and a session timezone name the chart does not know stops the study instead of falling back to America/New_York, because a zone name cannot be tested before it is used.

When the chart states no tick size, the original infers one from the median bar range of the whole chart, later bars included, which a study computed bar by bar cannot see; this version then uses a tick of 0.01, so its tick-based zone widths, pool tolerances, stop buffer and stop caps differ on such a chart.

A timezone that OpenScript does not recognise, such as an abbreviation like EST or a misspelt name, stops the study with an unknown-timezone error instead of falling back to another zone, because this version of OpenScript cannot test a zone name before using it.

Signal bars are shaded by counting whole chart intervals back from the chart clock rather than by counting bars, because a study cannot know on an earlier bar how many bars follow it, so on a market that closes, or when the clock is well past the newest bar, fewer bars are shaded; and the readout table sits in the nearest of four corners at the chart text size, because a table here has no centre positions and no size setting.

The Signal Level line is filled in 80 bars late and drawn back over the bars it covers, so the newest 80 bars never show it and a span longer than 81 bars shows only its last 81 bars, because a study cannot repaint earlier bars once a setup completes.

The break and retracement guide levels are drawn 120 bars after the bar they belong to, because a plot cannot write onto bars already drawn, so the newest 120 bars show no guide yet and a sequence longer than 120 bars loses its oldest part; with a Pivot Lookback Right above 5 each divergence point lands that many bars minus 5 after its pivot, because a plot's offset cannot be computed from a setting; the guides and the 60 and 40 band lines are solid, because a plot has no dotted style; and the table always sits bottom right at the standard text size, because a table offers only four corners and no text size.

The background shading is meant to cover signal bars among the newest Display Length bars, but a study cannot know in advance which bar will be the newest, so it counts whole chart intervals back from the chart's clock: on a market that closes, or when the clock is well past the newest bar, fewer bars are shaded, and where the chart supplies no clock none are.
